new_packages.label: בַּעַל דָּבָר, עַצְבוּת, וּמָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה
new_packages.reason: Torah #282's teaching is structured around an explicit good/evil polarity: the positive practice (finding good points → joy → song → prayer) is directly opposed by an evil force (the Adversary induces depression → the person despairs → cannot pray). The Rebbe names three concepts that share the same essential evil nature: בַּעַל דָּבָר (the Adversary), עַצְבוּת (sadness/depression), and מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה (melancholy/black bile). The text states that all of one's falls in mind and depression are 'רַק מַעֲשֵׂי בַּעַל דָּבָר' — they ARE the work of the Adversary. The Rebbe treats עצבות and מרה שחורה as effectively synonymous throughout ('מֵחֲמַת מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה וְעַצְבוּת' — always paired). The evil package is the structural mirror of Package 3 (the remaining good point) and Package 2 (the joy/melody): where Package 2 is the רוּחַ טוֹבָה (good spirit), the evil package is the רוּחַ נְכֵאָה (depressed spirit). The evil package also mirrors Package 1 (the tzaddik-shepherd): the בעל דבר is the anti-shepherd who pushes the person away from God rather than toward Him.

supporting_bechina_quotes.quote: עִקַּר רִחוּקָם הוּא מֵחֲמַת מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה וְעַצְבוּת
supporting_bechina_quotes.analysis: The Rebbe uses מרה שחורה and עצבות interchangeably throughout the text, treating them as the same essential evil state. They are two faces of the same depressive reality — not cause-and-effect but co-identical expressions.

supporting_bechina_quotes.quote: הַנְּפִילָה שֶׁבְּדַעְתּוֹ, וְהָעַצְבוּת וְהַמָּרָה שְׁחוֹרָה שֶׁנּוֹפֵל עָלָיו עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה, הַכֹּל הוּא רַק מַעֲשֵׂי בַּעַל דָּבָר
supporting_bechina_quotes.analysis: The Rebbe equates the depression with 'the acts of the Adversary' — the depression IS the work of the בעל דבר; they are the same essential evil phenomenon viewed from two angles. This is bechina language: 'הכל הוא רק מעשי בעל דבר' means the entire evil state IS the Adversary's nature.

new_packages.mirror_relationship: Evil mirror of Package 2 (joy/melody) and Package 3 (good point). Package 2's 'רוּחַ טוֹבָה' (good spirit) directly mirrors this package's 'רוּחַ נְכֵאָה עַצְבוּת רוּחַ' (spirit of sadness). The teaching explicitly names both: 'מְלַקֵּט הָרוּחַ טוֹבָה מִן הָרוּחַ נְכֵאָה עַצְבוּת רוּחַ' (he extracts the good spirit FROM the sad/depressed spirit).

observations:
Torah #282 DOES warrant one new package proposal: the evil cluster of {בעל דבר, עצבות, מרה שחורה}. This is not a marginal addition — it is the structural counterpart to the entire positive teaching, explicitly named by the Rebbe, and built from concepts that the text treats as bechina-equivalent (the depression IS the Adversary's work; sadness and melancholy are the same state). The three bechina pairs that would underpin this evil package are all present in the text's language but absent from the dataset:

1. עצבות ↔ מרה שחורה: always paired, treated as the same reality
2. בעל דבר ↔ עצבות: the Rebbe says the depression IS the Adversary's acts
3. רוח נכאה ↔ עצבות: already present in edge 1873's proof text ('הרוח נכאה עצבות רוח' — naming them as one)

The argument for this new package rests on the framework's principle (§4) that 'for nearly every cluster of good concepts, there is a corresponding cluster of evil concepts with the same structure.' Package 2's niggun/joy/extraction cluster demands an evil mirror — and the text provides it explicitly. The absence of bechina edges for this evil cluster in the current dataset represents a gap to be filled, not a reason to omit the package. The current dataset captures only the tip of Torah #282's conceptual structure.
